title: North America take-home ranking, 2026
persona: Single, no dependants, salary only, paid bi-weekly; no pre-tax savings; no city or county income tax.

method.canada: CanPay Insights engine: CRA T4032 (July 2026 edition) and Revenu Québec TP-1015.TI withholding — federal and provincial tax, CPP/QPP, EI, QPIP. Checked row by row against the official tables.
method.us: USAPay Insights engine: 2026 annual liability — federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, state income tax and statewide payroll contributions at their statutory employee rates.
method.basis: Canada is what the payroll withholds; the US is the tax owed for the year. For a single salary earner with no other income the two agree to within a few dollars.
method.fx: Bank of Canada daily USD/CAD, 249-day average 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-29: 1.3875. Canadian salaries are the US salary × this rate, rounded to the dollar.
method.ranks: By share of gross kept, shown to 0.1 point; jurisdictions that print the same share share a rank (1, 1, 3).

medians.note: Ranked within each country only: the two sources measure different things.

CA.source: Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0064-01, 2025: median hourly wage of full-time employees, all industries, × 2,080 hours, rounded to $100. Provinces only (no territorial series).

US.source: BLS OEWS May 2025, all occupations: median annual wage (hourly × 2,080).

DE: Delaware Paid Leave is modelled at the full-coverage employee maximum (0.4%); employers with 10–24 staff withhold at most 0.16% and those under 10 nothing
HI: Hawaii TDI (an employee-side deduction of up to 0.5% of weekly wages, capped) is NOT modelled: it is a private-insurance mandate under HRS ch. 392 and the employer may pay all of it or split it — the deduction is an employer choice with no statutory default, unlike the state-run funds above
the deduction rises again in 2028, 2030 and 2031 and the brackets in 2027 and 2029 — re-check each January
ME: Maine Paid Family & Medical Leave is modelled at the 0.5% employee maximum; an employer may absorb part or all of it
MD: all 24 county/city rates ARE modelled, opt-in via the city/county selector; without a selection, Maryland take-home is overstated by 2.25%–3.30% of taxable income
MI: Detroit's city income tax is modelled; the 23 other Michigan cities with an income tax are not
MN: Minnesota Paid Leave is modelled at the 0.44% employee maximum; an employer may choose to absorb part or all of it
MO: Kansas City and St. Louis earnings taxes are modelled for residents; non-residents working in either city are not
NH: no tax on wages; the interest-and-dividends tax was repealed and never applied to wage income
NY: NYC and Yonkers resident taxes ARE modelled, opt-in via the city/county selector; without a selection, city residents are overstated
OH: Ohio has roughly 600 taxing municipalities; the 17 largest are modelled and the rest are not — select a city to include it
OR: Portland-area taxes not included: Multnomah County Preschool for All (1.5% of county taxable income above $125,000 single / $200,000 joint, another 1.5% above $250,000 / $400,000) and Metro Supportive Housing (1%, thresholds inflation-indexed from 2026), per portland.gov/revenue; TriMet and Lane transit taxes are paid by employers, not withheld
Workers' Benefit Fund assessment not included: 0.9 cents per hour worked withheld from the employee in 2026 (DCBS, OAR 436-070), about $19 a year full-time; it is charged per hour, not on salary
PA: Philadelphia wage tax IS modelled (opt-in); other PA municipal earned income taxes (commonly ~1%) are not
HSA and cafeteria-plan treatment follows federal here; confirm against PA DOR before relying on it
VT: Child Care Contribution is modelled at the 0.11% employee maximum; an employer may pay all of it
WA: Washington taxes capital gains at 7%/9% but levies no tax on wage income
Workers' compensation employee share not included: L&I withholds part of the premium per hour worked, at a rate set by industry risk class
